definitions.explanation: Describes a material that is thicker than the standard version — typically used for fabrics, paper, cardboard, and ceramic dishware. Usually appears as {厚手|あつで}の + noun.

examples.japanese: {厚手|あつで}のセーターを{着|き}た。
この{紙|かみ}は{厚手|あつで}で{丈夫|じょうぶ}だ。
examples.english: This paper is thick and durable.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}は{厚手|あつで}のカーテンに{替|か}えると{部屋|へや}が{暖|あたた}かくなる。
examples.english: In winter, switching to thick curtains makes the room warmer.

notes:
Compound of {厚|あつ} (thick) + {手|で} (here a suffix indicating quality/grade of material).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {厚手|あつで}の{生地|きじ}: thick fabric
- {厚手|あつで}の{紙|かみ}: thick paper / heavyweight paper
- {厚手|あつで}のコート: a heavy coat
- {厚手|あつで}の{靴下|くつした}: thick socks
- {厚手|あつで}の{食器|しょっき}: heavyweight dishes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {薄手|うすで}: thin; lightweight — the direct opposite
- {分厚|ぶあつ}い: thick (more general, can describe books, walls, etc.)
